question: Why does a scratch rust faster on a tinned steel can than on a galvanised steel bucket?
answer: Zinc corrodes in the steel's place; tin makes the steel corrode instead. Where zinc and iron touch in wet air, zinc gives up electrons first, protecting even a bare scratch. Tin corrodes less readily than iron, so at a scratch the exposed iron dissolves, faster than on an uncoated can.
move: A protective layer can make the damage worse wherever it breaks.
source: Jones, Principles and Prevention of Corrosion, 1996
reference: Jones, Principles and Prevention of Corrosion, 2nd edition, Prentice Hall, 1996
